column2: integer ALU op on a tagged register
column11: the result is an UNTAGGED integer: a non-capability result commits with cap_result.valid = 0, so commit writes metadata 0 / tag 0 into the capability lane beside the value and the register file writes both lanes under one enable (we_gpr); a later LDC/STC/CJALR through rd is 24; to move a capability's cursor use CINCOFFSET/CINCOFFSETIMM (tag kept). NO integer-form instruction preserves a tag: the only writers of a tagged register are the FLU/DYN write-back ports (scoreboard ports 0 and 4: MOVC, CINCOFFSET(IMM), SCC, SHRINK(TO), TIGHTEN, SPLIT, SEAL, INIT, MREV, DELIN, CDERIVE, LDC, CALL/RETURN, the mints; every other port writes cap_result 0), CCSRRW's capability-CSR read, and the switcher's register writes; a plain ld of a capability granule is untagged too (S-14), as is a CSR read or an FP move. A static gate may refuse an LDC/STC/CJALR whose base was last defined by a scalar ALU op, a plain load, a CSR read or an FP move. QEMU does the same (translate.c:439-440, 462-463 clear the tag on every integer write)

column10: none: a plain jump executes with ANY rs1, tagged or not; the branch unit sets no PC metadata for it (only CJALR, and CBNZ when taken, do), so the PC capability keeps its current bounds and only the cursor moves
column11: an untagged rs1 is a plain integer target (no 24: there is no operand check on JALR). The target is then checked at commit against the CURRENT PCC when priv is M with capmode (a CSRUNV context runs at M with capmode): outside its bounds 28, no X permission 27, a non-LIN/NONLIN PCC 26, a dead PCC 25; inside the bounds a plain jump. QEMU 3b8040d5ff6e CHECKS THE SAME for every virtual-C block (capstone_supervisor.c:982-1062 pcc_fetch_cause / helper_capstone_check_pcc_block; translate.c:1425-1433 ends a block before an unfetchable instruction; tests/virtual-capstone-runtime pcc_bounds, fetch_full_width, cap_execute, revoked_pcc, revoked_cached_pcc prove it), with two residual differences: QEMU tests liveness FIRST (25 before 26/27/28) where the RTL tests it LAST, visible only when two conditions hold at once; and QEMU checks only virtual-C blocks, so the legacy-C monitor's own PCC is unchecked there and checked on silicon. (A first wording of this row said QEMU had no fetch check; retracted 2026-10-18.)
